call_timeout.meaning: Default bound on one whole call, including preparation and retries.

http_attempt_timeout.meaning: Default bound on one HTTP attempt, including login.

ws_request_timeout.meaning: Default wait for the reply to one WebSocket request.

ws_connect_timeout.meaning: Bound on one WebSocket connect, login and handshake included; also how long a request waits for a connection.

ws_idle_timeout.meaning: No frame of any kind (data, ping or pong) for this long means the connection is dead: drop it and reconnect. The client pings every third of it, so a quiet but healthy connection always has pongs.

ws_max_incoming_frame.meaning: Largest WebSocket frame the client accepts (64 MiB); a larger one closes the connection.

resync_timeout.meaning: Default wait for a fresh snapshot after a gap re-subscribe before reconnecting.

watchdog_interval.meaning: How often each WebSocket checks for an overdue resync, a rotated session and an idle connection, and sends its ping.

queue_size.meaning: Default bound on each subscription's queue.

read_attempts.meaning: Tries in total for a read that keeps failing with a retryable error. Writes are sent once.

read_backoff_base.meaning: Full-jitter backoff between read retries: wait uniform(0, min(cap, base * 2^attempt)).

reconnect_backoff_base.meaning: Full-jitter backoff between WebSocket reconnects, same formula as reads.

reconnect_backoff_reset_after.meaning: A connection that stayed up this long resets the reconnect backoff.

session_renew_at.meaning: Log in again once this share of the session cookie's lifetime has passed.

session_default_lifetime.meaning: Session lifetime assumed when the cookie carries no expiry.

session_retry_delay.meaning: Wait before trying a failed session renewal again.

session_renew_min_wait.meaning: Shortest wait before a session renewal, so a cookie that is already due does not log in again in a tight loop.

client_order_id_seconds_bits.meaning: Generated client order IDs are 1<<63 | seconds<<counter_bits | counter; seconds is the Unix time masked to this many bits.

client_order_id_counter_bits.meaning: Width of the per-process counter in the low bits of a generated client order ID.

countdown_min_seconds.meaning: Smallest countdown the cancel-on-disconnect helper accepts.

countdown_max_seconds.meaning: Largest countdown the cancel-on-disconnect helper accepts.

rate_limit_code.meaning: The rate-limit error code. A read always retries on it.

read_retry_statuses.meaning: HTTP statuses a read retries on, whatever the error code. Codes the contract marks retryable retry too.

write_rejected_statuses.meaning: Inclusive range. A write error is a definite rejection only if its HTTP status (when there is one) and its code's contract status are in it and the code is in the contract; otherwise the outcome is unknown.

options.name: idle_timeout
options.meaning: Silence after which a WebSocket connection is dropped. An advanced setting: keep it well above the server's 5 s ping interval, since the TypeScript SDK can't ping and relies on the server's pings.

extras.go: 0 means the default, since a Config field starts at 0; a negative value is a ConfigError.
extras.rust: Below watchdog_interval is a config error: the idle check runs once per watchdog tick, and the client pings every third of the timeout.

options.name: queue_size
options.meaning: Bound on each subscription's queue. It is one value for the client: for a different size, use a second client.

extras.go: 0 means the default, since a Config field starts at 0; a negative value is a ConfigError.

errors.meaning: The server answered with an error code. message is the server's text.

extras.typescript: Error.message is taken by the full text, so the server's text is serverMessage.

extras.go: Its own struct that unwraps to an *APIError, so errors.As finds both.
extras.rust: One enum, grvt::Error, with a variant per kind, so parents don't apply.

errors.meaning: No usable answer; sent says whether the request may have left.
A write may or may not have reached the exchange; it wraps the original failure.
An order leg breaks its instrument's limits; nothing was sent.

extras.python: Also a ValueError, as before it had its own class.

errors.meaning: The consumer fell behind a stream that may not drop items.
A WebSocket request is larger than the environment's frame limit; nothing was sent. Not a transport error: sending it again fails the same way.
A response or stream frame did not match its type.
A request could not be signed (missing field, over-precise decimal); nothing was sent.

extras.python: Also a ValueError, which signing raised before.
extras.typescript: DecimalError extends it with the decimal's details.

errors.meaning: A bad option, or the client lacks something the call needs (signer, API key).

extras.python: Also a ValueError, which bad options raised before.

extras.go: A sentinel error value, checked with errors.Is.

errors.meaning: The server repeated a cursor during a traversal.
The local order book must be rebuilt from a fresh snapshot.

extras.rust: Its own struct, returned by the order book helper, not a grvt::Error variant.

events.when: A WebSocket connected for the first time.
A WebSocket connected again after its connection was lost.
A WebSocket connection closed. code is the close code, when there is one.
The gateway answered a subscribe, after the first one or a re-subscribe.
A subscription may have missed items. gap holds the bounds; expected_prev, prev and seq describe a sequence_mismatch only.
A read failed and is tried again after delay (rpc is set), or a WebSocket connect failed and is tried again (socket is set). attempt counts from 1.
Every WebSocket frame sent or received, raw and not redacted.

extras.go: Outgoing is true for a sent frame: a bool instead of a direction.

events.when: A session renewal logged in. Authenticated WebSockets reconnect with the new cookie; this says nothing about missed items.

Something failed outside a call. fatal: a WebSocket stopped for good after its handshake or login was refused. Not fatal: a session renewal failed (no socket; error starts with "session: ") and is tried again after session_retry_delay.

extras.python: Also a non-fatal error when a WebSocket's read loop fails unexpectedly, before it reconnects.
